Shape Up 是 Basecamp 公司公开的一套产品开发方法，作者 Rya: Shape Up is the product development method Basecamp has published openly; its author, Ryan Singer, was head of product there. The question it answers: how can a small team avoid sinking into an endless backlog and still ship complete work on time?
核心是三步。第一步“塑形”：由有经验的人先把要做的事想到合适的粗细程度，定下“胃: The core is three steps. First, “shaping”: experienced people think the work through to the right level of detail and set the “appetite”, meaning how much time they're willing to spend on it, rather than first estimating how long it will take; then they sketch a rough solution, find the “rabbit holes” it could fall into, and write it up as a pitch. Second, “betting”: before each cycle starts, decide which pitches to bet on. Pitches not chosen don't go into a backlog; if someone still wants them, they pitch again next time. Third, “building”: hand the whole piece of work to a small team, let them break it into tasks themselves, and finish within six weeks. If it isn't done, by default it doesn't get extended; this is the “circuit breaker”. Each six-week cycle is followed by a two-week cool-down for fixes and planning what's next.
它最值得学的是“胃口”这个想法：先定时间，再在时间里决定做多少，而不是先定功能再: The idea most worth learning is “appetite”: fix the time first, then decide how much to do within it, instead of fixing the features first and then racing to finish. It works for content teams too.

“胃口”和“估时”有什么区别？: What's the difference between “appetite” and an estimate?
估时是先定做什么，再问要多久；胃口是先定愿意花多久，再决定在这段时间里做到什么程: An estimate fixes what to build, then asks how long it will take. Appetite fixes how long you're willing to spend, then decides how far to take it in that time.
待办池越积越长，只会制造焦虑和假承诺。没被选中的提案，真重要的话下个周期还会有人: A backlog only grows, creating anxiety and false promises. If a pitch that wasn't chosen really matters, someone will pitch it again next cycle.
一个项目六周内没做完，默认就停下，不自动延期。逼着塑形阶段把范围想清楚，也防止一: If a project isn't finished in six weeks, it stops by default instead of being extended automatically. That forces the scope to be thought through during shaping, and stops a project dragging on forever.
山形图的上坡和下坡分别是什么？: What are the uphill and downhill sides of a hill chart?
上坡是还在想办法、有未知；下坡是办法已经清楚、只剩执行。卡在上坡太久，说明问题没: Uphill means you're still working out the approach and there are unknowns; downhill means the approach is clear and only execution is left. Stuck uphill too long means the problem hasn't been thought through.
